resources.string: Prune\'s automated tests run in this environment.
Dedicated rules exist and the debloat engine is tested on stock Android, but not on this brand\'s hardware yet.
Dedicated rules and known firmware limitations are built in, tested only with simulated devices. Expect surprises: review every change.
No dedicated integration. The generic Android rules and the community database are used.
Settings → About phone → tap Build number 7 times (enter your PIN). Developer options appear in Settings → System.
Settings → About phone → Software information → tap Build number 7 times (enter your PIN).
Developer options are at the bottom of Settings.
Recent One UI versions block `pm disable-user` for some Samsung packages (\"Shell cannot change component state\"). Prune can uninstall them for the current user instead; that is reversible too.
Rooting a Galaxy phone trips Knox permanently: Samsung Wallet, Secure Folder and Samsung Health stop working. Prune never needs root.
Pixels have little manufacturer bloat. Most removable packages are Google apps: enable \"Include Google apps\" in a profile to see them.
Settings → About phone → tap OS version (HyperOS) or MIUI version 7 times.
Developer options are in Settings → Additional settings.

In Developer options also turn on \"USB debugging (Security settings)\". Without it Xiaomi blocks permission, background and animation changes over ADB/Shizuku. Xiaomi requires a SIM card and a Xiaomi account to turn it on.
Needed for `pm grant/revoke`, app-ops and settings changes. Disabling and removing apps works without it.
HyperOS/MIUI updates sometimes re-enable or reinstall removed system apps. Run your profile again after an update.
Removing the Security app, permission manager or core MIUI packages can bootloop: Prune keeps them locked.
EMUI and HarmonyOS refuse `pm disable-user` for many system apps. Prune falls back to uninstalling for the current user, which is reversible.
This phone runs without Google Mobile Services. Huawei Mobile Services (HMS Core) and AppGallery replace them, so Prune keeps both locked.
Prune works on HarmonyOS versions that still run Android apps (2.x to 4.x). HarmonyOS NEXT cannot run Android apps at all.
Huawei Mobile Services: this phone has no Google services, so apps depend on HMS Core.
AppGallery: the only app store on this phone (no Google Play).
MagicOS refuses `pm disable-user` for many system apps. Prune falls back to uninstalling for the current user, which is reversible.
Honor Mobile Services replace Google services on this phone, so Prune keeps them locked.
Honor Mobile Services: this phone has no Google services, so apps depend on it.
Settings → About device → Version → tap Build number 7 times.
Developer options are in Settings → Additional settings (System settings on newer versions).
In Developer options turn on \"Disable permission monitoring\". Without it permission and background changes over ADB/Shizuku are refused.
ColorOS-based firmware blocks `pm grant/revoke` and app-op changes until this developer option is on.
The Security Center and permission manager are locked: removing them breaks permission dialogs.
Motorola ships many configuration overlays (Wi-Fi, SIM, audio). They are locked or high risk: some cause bootloops when removed.
Settings → About phone → tap Build number 7 times (the exact place varies by manufacturer).
